finding.claim: PUT /me mass-assigns the entire request body onto req.user via Object.assign, then persists it with req.store.save, letting any authenticated user overwrite arbitrary stored fields (e.g. role/isAdmin, tenant, id) depending on the user model.

trace.note: router.put("/me") accepts the request with no field allowlist
Object.assign copies every own key of req.body onto req.user, including __proto__ which sets the object's prototype
req.store.save persists the mutated user object
updated record is echoed back in the response

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist or field filter on the /me route. Sibling route /me/profile (users.js:11-12) does allowlist displayName and bio, so the /me route is the unprotected one. Auth middleware and user schema are outside the repo and could not be verified; which fields are dangerous is UNCERTAIN.

verdict.guard_found: No allowlist or filter on the PUT /me route (users.js:4-7). The only visible control is the sibling /me/profile route (users.js:11-12), which allowlists displayName and bio, but it does not guard /me. The auth middleware and req.store are not in the repo (the only file is users.js), so nothing else was found.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: users.js:5 runs Object.assign(req.user, req.body) with no allowlist, and users.js:6 persists the result. Whether an authenticated user can escalate depends on fields in the user model and the store's save behavior (users.js:6), and neither is in the repo, so the privilege impact cannot be confirmed.
